newsitem.title: USA: Jones says Q1 showed strong growth.
newsitem.headline: Jones says Q1 showed strong growth.

text.p: Jones Medical Industries Inc said first-quarter 1997 results showed strong growth of hospital pharmaceutical sales and physician driven prescription pharmaceutical sales.

The company on Thursday reported net income for the first quarter of $8.1 million, or $0.28 per share on sales of $29.8 million, compared to net income of $3.7 million, or $0.15 per share, on sales of $21.8 million in the same quarter of 1996.

The company's higher margin pharmaceutical products accounted for 75 percent of sales, resulting in an increase in gross profit to 70 percent of sales compared to 57 percent during the 1996 first quarter, Jones said.
Operating income also increased to 42.8 percent of sales compared to 28.5 percent a year ago, Jones said.
In related news, Jones said a recent medical study could boost sales of the company's Levoxyl, a generic form of levothyroxine for treating hypothyroidism.
The Journal of the American Medical Association last week published a study that compared the bioequivalence of certain levothyroxine products, including Levoxyl.

"The study, conducted at the University of California Medical Center, San Francisco, concluded that Levoxyl and Synthroid, the $350 million U.S. market leader, 'are bioequivalent by current Food and Drug Administration criteria,'" Jones said.
